change.title: Explicit shard grants for svc_bundle_reader
change.diff:
--- /dev/null
+++ b/db/migrations/0042_reader_shard_grants.sql
@@ -0,0 +1,3 @@
+-- Make the reader's access to shard databases explicit so per-principal
+-- query limits and audit logging apply to it.
+GRANT SELECT ON r0.* TO svc_bundle_reader;

verdict.headline: Explicit shard grants for svc_bundle_reader breaks worker-runtime startup by exceeding max_entries=200
verdict.cause: The GRANT SELECT ON r0.* given to svc_bundle_reader causes the bundle-builder to discover and include metadata from both default.bundle_fields (140 entries) and r0.bundle_fields (140 entries), totaling 280 entries. The worker-runtime is configured with max_entries=200 (runtime_config:rc-0007), so 280 > 200 causes a fatal startup error: "bundle has 280 entries but the runtime preallocates 200; refusing to start"
tested: x-80e97cfbd0524372: baseline · workload default → all assertions passed
x-2d7d913a89c64299: candidate · workload default → failed: runtime_starts_with_bundle
x-5e0b5c4470d04fd9: candidate · workload default → failed: runtime_starts_with_bundle
x-d056ce4d223c4220: control · workload default → all assertions passed
limitations: Could not test per-principal query limit enforcement separately; could not observe audit logging behavior change; only tested default workload

mitigation.text: Remove the explicit GRANT SELECT ON r0.* from the change, or reduce worker-runtime.max_entries from 200 to >= 280 (if 280 entries is the intended capacity), or ensure the bundle-builder only queries bundle_fields in one database rather than both default and r0

Run the candidate with the explicit shard grants to observe differences
Harness confirmation: candidate run required before the judge can call a reproduced failure.
Harness confirmation: control run required before the judge can call a reproduced failure.

hypotheses.claim: The explicit grant may allow svc_bundle_reader to query additional tables in database r0 beyond bundle_fields, triggering per-principal query limits. However, the experiment shows the failure is specifically due to max_entries being exceeded (280 > 200), not due to per-principal query limit throttling. The runtime exits with code 2 because of entry count overflow, not query limit violations.
hypotheses.mechanism: The failure mechanism is max_entries overflow, not per-principal query limit enforcement. The explicit grant r0.* provides access to all tables in r0, but the observed failure is the entries limit, not query limits.

hypotheses.claim: The explicit shard grant for svc_bundle_reader on database r0 causes the bundle-builder to read metadata from both default.bundle_fields AND r0.bundle_fields, doubling the entries from 140 to 280 and exceeding the worker-runtime max_entries=200 limit, causing runtime startup failure.
hypotheses.mechanism: The GRANT SELECT ON r0.* gives svc_bundle_reader access to all tables in r0, including r0.bundle_fields. Combined with existing access to default.bundle_fields, the bundle-builder now discovers 280 total rows (140 from each database) instead of 140. The worker-runtime is configured with max_entries=200, so 280 > 200 causes the fatal error.

hypotheses.claim: The explicit shard grant for svc_bundle_reader on database r0 could bypass audit logging that was previously enforced on the implicit principal access, creating an audit blind spot for queries originating from bundle-builder.
hypotheses.mechanism: Previously, svc_bundle_reader accessed shard databases implicitly, which may have been covered by audit logging on the implicit principal. Making the grant explicit could change how audit systems track the principal, or the audit system may have been configured for the implicit access pattern and not the explicit grant.
